name: Ananias of Damascus
charge: Going to the street called Straight and putting his hands on the man who had come to bind him: Brother Saul
summary: Saul was still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples and had gone to the high priest for letters to Damascus, so that any of this way, men or women, could be brought bound to Jerusalem. A disciple at Damascus named Ananias was told in a vision to go to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas, and lay hands on Saul of Tarsus. He answered that he had heard by many how much evil this man had done to the saints at Jerusalem and that he held authority from the chief priests, and he was told to go, because Saul was a chosen vessel. He went in, called him Brother Saul, and laid his hands on him.
offenseFull: Saul was still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord and went to the high priest for letters to the synagogues at Damascus, so that if he found any of this way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem (Acts 9:1-2). Before the followers of Christ were called Christians at Antioch they were called this way, meaning the way of Christ; and the sisters were hunted with the men, so this was not a persecution of the men only. These letters came from the same office that had the Messiah put to death, so it is no surprise that they were now having his disciples killed. On the road the light shone and the voice asked why he persecuted him; Saul never laid a hand on the Messiah himself, but he was laying hands on the elect, and to persecute the elect is to persecute Christ. Then the Lord spoke in a vision to a certain disciple at Damascus named Ananias and sent him to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas, to ask for Saul of Tarsus, who was praying and had himself seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in and putting his hand on him (Acts 9:3-12).

Ananias objected, saying he had heard by many of this man, how much evil he had done to the saints at Jerusalem, and that here he had authority from the chief priests to bind all that called on the name (Acts 9:13-14). The objection was honest: this man held what amounted to a licence to kill from the high priest, and he had consented to Stephen’s death, shut up the saints in prison, punished them in every synagogue, and persecuted them even to strange cities (Acts 26:10-11). Was Saul doing it in ignorance? He was, and that is why the scripture says to judge nothing before the time (1 Corinthians 4:5). The scriptures and the power of the spirit can fix the worst of us, the murderers, the thieves, the covetous, the adulterers, and the fornicators. Paul later called himself a blasphemer, a persecutor, and injurious, and said he obtained mercy because he did it ignorantly in unbelief (1 Timothy 1:13). This is the true meaning of loving your enemies (Matthew 5:43-45): not the ones who enslaved and colonized your ancestors, which is what Christianity twists it into, but the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies, and he could still repent.

The Lord told Ananias to go his way, because Saul was a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel, and that he would be shown how great things he must suffer for that name (Acts 9:15-16). Ananias went his way and entered into the house, and putting his hands on him called him Brother Saul, saying that the Lord, even Jesus, who had appeared to him in the way, had sent him so that he might receive his sight and be filled with the Holy Ghost (Acts 9:17). He had heard the report and stated the danger, and then he obeyed anyway.
judgmentFull: Something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, he received sight, arose, and was baptized; and he spent certain days with the disciples at Damascus, and straightway preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God (Acts 9:18-20). At that time there was no New Testament, so he preached Christ out of the law and the prophets and confounded the Jews that dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ (Acts 9:22). People discredit Paul’s writings, but Acts credits and justifies them, so to throw out Paul a man would have to throw out Acts with him. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly, which is why he told the Galatians that he neither received the gospel of man nor was taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ (Galatians 1:11-12).

Paul kept the man in his own account years later, calling Ananias a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews that dwelt at Damascus, who told him that the God of our fathers had chosen him to know his will, and to see the Just One, and to be his witness of what he had seen and heard (Acts 22:12-16). A devout man is a man according to the laws of the Most High who has a good report, and that is the measure by which Ananias is remembered: not by his fear, but by his keeping of the law and by the name he gave the man the whole congregation was afraid of.

taught.title: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law
Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

text.text: And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,
And desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.
And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:
And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.
And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.
And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord.
And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth,
And hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight.
Then Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem:
And here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on thy name.
Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall every man have praise of God.
Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.
But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel:
For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.

And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.
And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
And when he had received meat, he was strengthened. Then was Saul certain days with the disciples which were at Damascus.
And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.
But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.
But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.
For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.
And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,
Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
